_comment: Storyboard for the Grade 2 Science unit lecture film, Lesson 4 Natural or Made?. Rendered by tools/create-ehel-unit-lecture.js. See lecture-video/BRIEF.md. Every beat is one narration clip; art.at names the phrases a picture waits for, and the page refuses to load if a phrase is not in its beat's say. The five teaching chapters are the five parts of LESSON["lecture"] in content/lesson-4.py, in their order and in the lesson's own words: wood, wool and stone (its explore cards); plastic, glass, brick and paper made in factories, glass from melted sand and paper from wood pulp, and the sort step's one question; the material tester's four tests on glass and then wool; the drip test and the record step's table; and the context step's kettle and tyre.
title: Natural or Made?
subtitle: Grade 2 Science
objectives: Understand that some materials occur naturally and others are manufactured.
Describe a property as a characteristic of a material and understand that materials can have more than one property.
Explain why materials are chosen for specific purposes on the basis of their properties.
Know that materials can be tested to determine their properties.
Sort and group objects, materials and living things based on observations of the similarities and differences between them.
Collect and record observations and/or measurements by annotating images and completing simple tables.
Talk about how science explains how objects they use, or know about, work.

beats.say: Some materials come from nature. Others are made by people.
You will test materials, and find out why each one is chosen.
Wood comes from trees. It grows, so it is natural.
Wool comes from sheep. It grows, and is cut off and spun. It is natural.
Stone is dug out of the ground. It is natural too.
A natural material grows, or it is dug up. People do not make it.
Plastic, glass, brick and paper are made by people, in factories.
Glass is made by melting sand, very hot. The sand becomes glass.
Paper is made in a factory, by mashing wood into pulp.
These are manufactured: made by people, usually in a factory.
To sort a material, ask one question: could you find it in nature?
A property is what a material is like. You can test for each one.
Test the glass. Press it: it is hard. Bend it: it is stiff.
Hold it to the light: it is see-through. Pour water on it: waterproof.
Glass is hard, stiff, see-through and waterproof, all at once.
Now test wool. It is soft, and it bends easily. Different answers!
Each test finds one property. A material has several.
Drip water on glass, and the water runs off.
Drip water on wool, and the water soaks in.
Glass is waterproof: water does not go through it.
Wool is absorbent: it soaks water up.
You will record each result in a table. Glass: yes. Wool: no.
Fill in a row for every material. Then you can compare them.
People choose a material for a job because of its properties.
A kettle is metal, because metal does not melt when it gets hot.
Its handle is plastic. Plastic does not carry the heat to your hand.
A tyre is rubber. Rubber grips the road and bends over bumps.
Every material is chosen for its properties. Science explains why.
Natural materials grow, or are dug up. People make the manufactured ones.
A property is what a material is like. Each test finds one of them.
Glass is waterproof. Wool is absorbent. You record both in a table.
Every material is chosen for its properties. Now go on a hunt of your own!
